subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests intentionally persist `/exec` defaults, but the reported behavior can shadow later operator security policy changes and affects upgrade/reset semantics.

options.title: Global policy upper bound
options.body: Make current global or agent exec policy cap or clear stored session exec fields, with tests and a doctor/reset path for existing session entries.

options.title: Keep persistence as-is
options.body: Preserve session-level `/exec` precedence and document the operational reset or diagnostic steps administrators must use after policy changes.

options.title: Add operator reset first
options.body: Ship a focused reset or doctor repair surface before changing resolver precedence so administrators can clear stale session exec state explicitly.

recommendation.title: Global policy upper bound
recommendation.body: Make current global or agent exec policy cap or clear stored session exec fields, with tests and a doctor/reset path for existing session entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The original `/exec` session override feature and focused resolver tests trace most clearly to this owner history.
